title.en: Newton's second law, momentum and impulse
title.kn: ನ್ಯೂಟನ್‌ನ ಎರಡನೇ ನಿಯಮ, ಸಂವೇಗ ಮತ್ತು ಆವೇಗ

hook.en: A fielder pulls his hands back while catching a fast ball. Stopping it over a longer time means a smaller force on his palms.
hook.kn: ವೇಗವಾದ ಚೆಂಡನ್ನು ಹಿಡಿಯುವಾಗ ಫೀಲ್ಡರ್ ಕೈಗಳನ್ನು ಹಿಂದಕ್ಕೆ ಎಳೆಯುತ್ತಾನೆ. ಹೆಚ್ಚು ಸಮಯದಲ್ಲಿ ನಿಲ್ಲಿಸಿದರೆ ಅಂಗೈಗಳ ಮೇಲೆ ಕಡಿಮೆ ಬಲ ಬೀಳುತ್ತದೆ.

narration.en: A fielder pulls his hands back while catching a fast ball. Stopping it over a longer time means a smaller force on his palms.
narration.kn: ವೇಗವಾದ ಚೆಂಡನ್ನು ಹಿಡಿಯುವಾಗ ಫೀಲ್ಡರ್ ಕೈಗಳನ್ನು ಹಿಂದಕ್ಕೆ ಎಳೆಯುತ್ತಾನೆ. ಹೆಚ್ಚು ಸಮಯದಲ್ಲಿ ನಿಲ್ಲಿಸಿದರೆ ಅಂಗೈಗಳ ಮೇಲೆ ಕಡಿಮೆ ಬಲ ಬೀಳುತ್ತದೆ.

body.en: Linear momentum is $\vec p = m\vec v$. The second law says the rate of change of momentum equals the net external force: $\vec F = d\vec p/dt$. For constant mass this becomes $\vec F = m\vec a$. The SI unit of force is the newton: 1 N = 1 kg m s⁻².
body.kn: ರೇಖೀಯ ಸಂವೇಗ p = mv. ಸಂವೇಗದ ಬದಲಾವಣೆಯ ದರವು ನಿವ್ವಳ ಬಾಹ್ಯ ಬಲಕ್ಕೆ ಸಮ: F = dp/dt. ಸ್ಥಿರ ದ್ರವ್ಯರಾಶಿಗೆ F = ma. ಬಲದ ಏಕಮಾನ ನ್ಯೂಟನ್.

points.en: Force and acceleration point the same way
Holds for each component: Fₓ = maₓ
F = 0 gives a = 0, the first law

body.en: Impulse is force multiplied by the time for which it acts, and it equals the change in momentum: $J = F\,\Delta t = \Delta p$. A large force acting for a very short time, such as a bat hitting a ball, is best described by its impulse. Increasing the stopping time reduces the force, which is why we use cushions, airbags and sand pits.
body.kn: ಆವೇಗ = ಬಲ × ಅದು ವರ್ತಿಸುವ ಕಾಲ = ಸಂವೇಗದ ಬದಲಾವಣೆ. ನಿಲ್ಲಿಸುವ ಕಾಲ ಹೆಚ್ಚಿಸಿದರೆ ಬಲ ಕಡಿಮೆಯಾಗುತ್ತದೆ; ಅದಕ್ಕೇ ಮೆತ್ತೆ, ಏರ್‌ಬ್ಯಾಗ್, ಮರಳು ಗುಂಡಿ ಬಳಸುತ್ತೇವೆ.

Area under the F–t graph = impulse

problem.en: A force of 10 N acts on a 2 kg body at rest for 3 s. Find its acceleration and final velocity.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. A force of 10 N acts on a 2 kg body at rest for 3 s. Find its acceleration and final velocity.

problem.en: A batsman hits a 0.15 kg ball straight back to the bowler without changing its speed of 12 m/s. Find the impulse given to the ball.

steps.en: Take the direction towards the batsman as positive: p_i = 0.15 × 12 = 1.8 kg m/s.
After the hit: p_f = −1.8 kg m/s.
Impulse = p_f − p_i = −3.6 N s, i.e. 3.6 N s towards the bowler.

answer.en: 3.6 N s, directed towards the bowler

narration.en: Let us solve this together. A batsman hits a 0.15 kg ball straight back to the bowler without changing its speed of 12 m/s. Find the impulse given to the ball.

body.en: If a body rebounds straight back with the same speed, the change in momentum is 2mv, not zero and not mv.

narration.en: Bounce back? Double it. If a body rebounds straight back with the same speed, the change in momentum is 2mv, not zero and not mv.

points.en: A longer stopping time means a smaller force.

homework.en: A 1500 kg car moving at 20 m/s stops in 5 s. Find the average braking force (answer: 6000 N).

narration.en: Recap. p = mv; F = dp/dt = ma. Impulse = FΔt = change in momentum. A longer stopping time means a smaller force.
narration.kn: ಪುನರಾವರ್ತನೆ. p = mv; F = dp/dt = ma. ಆವೇಗ = FΔt = ಸಂವೇಗದ ಬದಲಾವಣೆ. ನಿಲ್ಲಿಸುವ ಕಾಲ ಹೆಚ್ಚಾದರೆ ಬಲ ಕಡಿಮೆ.
